question: Is there a plugin registration conflict?
finding: CRITICAL. Theme repo contains THREE plugin copies: justice-core (uje_ prefix), ultra-justice-engine (uje_ prefix), ultra-justice (uj_ prefix). justice-core and ultra-justice-engine BOTH declare uje_register_practice_areas_taxonomy / uje_register_city_taxonomy / uje_register_lawyer_cpt -> activating both causes a fatal PHP redeclare error.
evidence: Code review of all three includes/ folders
recommended_fix: Keep exactly ONE plugin copy active. Decommission the other two folders from the repo after confirming the active plugin in wp-admin/plugins.php

question: Is load order causing taxonomy problems?
finding: Possible. CPT justice_lawyer registers at init priority 10 with taxonomies=>[practice-areas,city]; practice-areas taxonomy also registers at priority 10; city at priority 9. If the CPT registers before practice-areas, the CPT-side association can be skipped. Net effect on live is currently fine, but it is fragile.
evidence: Code review of cpt-lawyers.php + taxonomy-*.php hooks
recommended_fix: Fix applied: theme safety net at priority 99 makes the result deterministic regardless of plugin load order

question: Are there duplicate practice-area terms?
finding: Yes - legacy pollution confirmed. practice-areas contains old WordPress categories that were merged in: term 18 has a URL-encoded Hebrew slug (%d7%90%d7%92...) and an old /קטגוריות-מאמרים/ URL; term 640 (rabbinical-court) carries a full HTML article body as its description. Mix of clean English-slug terms (criminal-law 170, real-estate-law 713, national-insurance 717) and legacy terms.
evidence: Live REST /wp-json/wp/v2/practice-areas sample (full list truncated by tooling)
recommended_fix: Produce full term inventory, then map legacy terms -> canonical terms and plan a controlled merge (no deletes until mapped)

question: Is the practice-areas term naming consistent?
finding: No. Some terms have an English string as the display NAME (term 713 name = 'real-estate-law') instead of Hebrew. Slugs are mostly English but at least one is percent-encoded Hebrew (term 18).
recommended_fix: Normalise: Hebrew display name + clean lowercase English slug for every term

question: Are there duplicate or inconsistent city terms?
finding: 19 city terms total. 9 (ids 700-710) have Latin placeholder NAMES (e.g. name 'tel-aviv'); 10 (ids 719-728) have correct Hebrew names. No slug collisions, but front-end will display Latin names for 9 cities. Root cause: the 9 Latin terms were created first by an earlier import; inc/taxonomy-seed.php only inserts cities whose slug does not already exist, so it could not correct them.
evidence: Subagent extract of full city term list
recommended_fix: Rename the 9 Latin-named city terms to Hebrew display names (term names only; keep slugs and IDs to preserve URLs and assignments)
